1. Load your image.
2. Pick a ratio, or drag the orange handles out. To straighten a crooked picture, turn it with the round handle.
3. Optional: finish the sentence in **What goes there**.
4. Press **Run**.

The new area is painted with the outpaint LoRA, which keeps your picture where it is. Your original pixels go back on top at the end.

Pull out at most about your picture's own size on one side per run. For more, run again on the result.

The two boxes in the middle do the work. Double-click one to see inside.

If the run stops at a red **LoRA Loader**, the LoRA file is missing. Download it below, or switch its row off to run FLUX 3 without it. Without it the picture can zoom or slide instead of being extended.

Not happy with the new area? Run it again. The seed changes each run.

nodes.title: Note
widgets_values: Qwen3-VL, FLUX 3's own text encoder, describes your picture the way the LoRA's training captions were written, and adds what you typed in What goes there. It never sees the gray.

nodes.title: Instruction plus what goes there
widgets_values: Write the text-to-image prompt that would generate this exact picture. One paragraph of 50 to 90 words. Begin with the medium and style in a few words, such as "Photograph", "Smartphone photo", "Anime illustration", "Oil painting" or "3D render". Then describe the subject, the setting, and what fills every part of the frame from edge to edge, including the background and the areas near the borders. Any flat mid-gray parts, such as corners or a background, are blank space that will be painted to continue the scene: describe the scene as if it filled the whole frame, and don't describe a border, frame or vignette around it. Include materials, colours, lighting, time of day, camera angle and framing. Quote any readable text exactly. Use plain factual language; do not start with 'The image' or 'This picture' and do not give opinions. Output only the prompt.
